note: The 2005 BRCA synthetic-lethality prediction was tested prospectively in BRCA carriers in 2009 and held; the FDA's 2014 review matched the xenograft PK/PD dose threshold and the rat/dog marrow-toxicity signal to patients.
label: Ovarian cancer (PARP)

engagement.note: Inhibiting PARP enzymatic activity profoundly sensitised BRCA1/2-deficient cells, with chromosomal instability, arrest and apoptosis; no patient PAR data yet.
engagement.quote: We show here that BRCA1 or BRCA2 dysfunction unexpectedly and profoundly sensitizes cells to the inhibition of PARP enzymatic activity, resulting in chromosomal instability, cell cycle arrest and subsequent apoptosis.

engagement.note: Olaparib cut PAR in patients' blood cells, hair follicles and tumour biopsies at tolerated doses, as the cell model required; no side-by-side comparison stated.
engagement.quote: pharmacodynamic studies confirmed PARP inhibition in surrogate samples (of peripheral-blood mononuclear cells and plucked eyebrow-hair follicles) and tumor tissue.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level (NEJM paywalled). The trial was designed to test the 2005 cell prediction, but the engagement readout is a direct PD measurement; the paper does not tabulate model vs patient PAR. Called 'same' because the mechanism-level prediction (PAR loss at a tolerated exposure) was observed in patients. Registry NCT00516373 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-02).

dose.model: Brca1-/-;p53-/- mammary GEMM dosed with olaparib
dose.note: Olaparib inhibited Brca1-deficient mouse mammary tumours without toxicity; no exposure or PAR target was yet compared with patients.
dose.quote: Treatment of tumor-bearing mice with AZD2281 inhibited tumor growth without signs of toxicity, resulting in strongly increased survival.

dose.model: HBCx-10 TNBC patient-derived xenograft PK/PD (tumour PAR vs free plasma olaparib)
dose.note: FDA: unbound steady-state troughs at 200–400 mg BID exceeded the nonclinical IC90 for ≥90% PAR loss; only 400 mg put every patient above it.
dose.quote: Clinical unbound steady state trough concentrations in patients who received 200 and 400 mg BID olaparib exceeded the estimated IC90 values from nonclinical studies.
dose.judgement: Full review read (pp. 4-5, 41-42, 46). The IC90 comes from the applicant's HBCx-10 PDX PK/PD study (initiated 2011-11-25) plus a simulation that SSBs rise only when PAR falls >=90%; the comparison is retrospective integration, not a prospective prediction. Audeh 2010 (doi 10.1016/S0140-6736(10)60893-8; NCT00494442, results posted 2015-01-26) saw ORR 13% at 100 mg vs 33% at 400 mg BID, consistent with the threshold, but that juxtaposition is mine. Trough data pool several trials, so registry_date is null.

efficacy.note: BRCA2-deficient cells were acutely sensitive to PARP inhibitors and BRCA2-deficient xenografts were killed by PARP inhibition alone; no patient had been dosed.
efficacy.short: BRCA2-null tumours killed by PARP inhibition
efficacy.quote: We exploit this requirement in order to kill BRCA2-deficient tumours by PARP inhibition alone.

efficacy.note: Phase 1 built to test the 2005 synthetic-lethality prediction: responses occurred only in BRCA carriers (ovarian, breast, prostate), none in non-carriers.
efficacy.quote: Objective antitumor activity was reported only in mutation carriers, all of whom had ovarian, breast, or prostate cancer and had received multiple treatment regimens.
efficacy.judgement: Clean prospective test: Bryant/Farmer (Apr 2005) preceded first dosing (NCT00516373 start 2005-07-11) and the 2009 report. Abstract-level (NEJM paywalled); comparison_stated=true because the paper frames itself as a test of the synthetic-lethal hypothesis, not a numeric side-by-side. Not 'neg': Murai 2012 (doi 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-12-2753, full text read) ranked veliparib the weakest PARP trapper and ~10-fold less cytotoxic in BRCA2-deficient cells, and veliparib monotherapy 400 mg BID gave ORR 26% in gBRCA ovarian cancer (Coleman 2015, doi 10.1016/j.ygyno.2015.03.042; NCT01540565 results posted 2019-03-19) vs 33% for olaparib 400 mg BID (Audeh 2010), but VELIA (Coleman 2019, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1909707; NCT02470585 results posted 2020-09-14) was positive (BRCA cohort HR 0.44), so no drug of the class failed in this population; the weaker-trapper juxtaposition is mine, not stated by any single source. Not 'contra': NOVA (Mirza 2016, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1611310; NCT01847274 results posted 2019-05-01) found niraparib benefit also in non-gBRCA/HRD-negative patients, which the model did not predict, but that lies outside this context's population.

safety.note: PARP1-/- mice are viable and fertile and BRCA-proficient cells tolerate PARP inhibition, predicting a tumour-selective, chemotherapy-sparing profile; myelosuppression not modelled.
safety.quote: Nevertheless, PARP1-/- mice are viable, fertile and do not develop early onset tumours.

safety.note: Olaparib spared patients most chemotherapy toxicities, as the selectivity model predicted; dose-limiting thrombocytopenia and CNS effects at 400–600 mg BID were not modelled.
safety.quote: Olaparib has few of the adverse effects of conventional chemotherapy, inhibits PARP, and has antitumor activity in cancer associated with the BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.
safety.judgement: Abstract-level. The selectivity prediction held (no excess toxicity in carriers, few chemotherapy-type effects), but the cell/knockout model was silent on the grade 4 thrombocytopenia and mood/somnolence DLTs; those were caught by animal toxicology (next entry).

safety.note: Rat/dog toxicology named the hematopoietic system as the target organ (at 2–4% of clinical AUC); patients at 400 mg BID showed anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia.
safety.short: Animal marrow toxicity matched clinical cytopenias
safety.quote: In humans, olaparib caused hematological toxicities, including anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and lymphopenia at the recommended clinical dose of 400 mg twice daily.
safety.judgement: Full review read (p. 16, p. 138). Second consecutive 'same' kept because the best safety model changed (animal toxicology, not the selectivity cell model) and it carries the filed-model facts; prune if the one-entry-per-status-change rule is strict. Direction matched but magnitude did not: the preceding sentences state cytopenias in rats and dogs at >=2% and 4% of clinical exposure, i.e. animals were >25x more sensitive on AUC, which the reviewer notes without calling a miss. Hopkins 2019 (doi 10.1158/1541-7786.MCR-18-0138; epub 2018-11-14) later tied marrow cytotoxicity to trapping potency and called it 'consistent with emerging clinical data' (abstract only; full text 403-blocked), explaining class-wide thrombocytopenia/anemia without changing the status.
